answer: Like a lantern hung at a crossroads, an agent economy can require each identity to carry a signed receipt of completed, independently verifiable work before it earns anything. A new agent must wander through a randomized benchmark task checked by strangers, then lock a small stake that is slashed if its behavior mirrors another identity. Each clone then costs real compute plus locked capital, and a plume of cheap copies collapses the moment their receipts repeat. Limits: a rich attacker can still buy many receipts, so verification must stay random and stake must scale with earnings.
